text: Again he went into a synagogue, and a man with a withered hand was there.
They watched him closely to see whether he would heal the man on the Sabbath, so that they could bring a charge against him.
He said to the man with the withered hand, "Stand up here in front of everyone."
Then he asked them, "Is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good or to do harm, to save a life or to kill?" But they said nothing.
He looked around at them in anger, deeply grieved at their hardness of heart, and said to the man, "Stretch out your hand." He stretched it out, and his hand was restored.
Then the Pharisees went out and immediately began plotting with the Herodians how to destroy him.
Jesus withdrew with his disciples to the sea, and a great crowd from Galilee followed him. They came also from Judea,

versions.text: Jesus withdrew with his disciples to the sea, and a great crowd followed him from Galilee. From Judea as well,
versions.explanation: "From Judea as well," leaves the verse ending on a bare fragment, which is hard to read aloud. Recasting it as a clause with a verb keeps the sentence running smoothly into verse 8 without changing the sense.

text: and from Jerusalem, Idumea, the region beyond the Jordan, and the area around Tyre and Sidon, a great multitude came to him, for they had heard all that he was doing.
He told his disciples to have a small boat ready for him, to keep the crowd from crushing him;
for he had healed so many that all who had diseases were pressing in on him to touch him.
And whenever the unclean spirits saw him, they fell down before him and cried out, "You are the Son of God!"
But he sternly warned them again and again not to make him known.
Then he went up on the mountain and called to himself those he wanted, and they came to him.
He appointed twelve, so that they might be with him and that he might send them out to preach,
and to have authority to drive out demons.
These are the twelve he appointed: Simon, to whom he gave the name Peter;
James son of Zebedee and his brother John (to them he gave the name Boanerges, that is, Sons of Thunder);
Andrew, Philip, Bartholomew, Matthew, Thomas, James son of Alphaeus, Thaddaeus, Simon the Cananean,
and Judas Iscariot, who betrayed him.
Then he went home, and the crowd gathered again, so that they could not even eat.
When his family heard about it, they went out to take charge of him, for they were saying, "He is out of his mind."
And the scribes who had come down from Jerusalem said, "He is possessed by Beelzebul," and, "It is by the ruler of the demons that he drives out demons."
So he called them to him and spoke to them in parables: "How can Satan drive out Satan?
If a kingdom is divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand.
And if a household is divided against itself, that household will not be able to stand.
So if Satan has risen up against himself and is divided, he cannot stand; his end has come.
No one can enter a strong man's house and plunder his goods unless he first ties up the strong man; then he can plunder his house.
Truly I tell you, people will be forgiven every sin and every blasphemy they utter;
but whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will never have forgiveness; he is guilty of an eternal sin."
He said this because they were saying, "He has an unclean spirit."
Then his mother and his brothers came, and standing outside, they sent word to him, calling for him.
A crowd was sitting around him, and they told him, "Look, your mother and your brothers are outside, looking for you."

versions.text: A crowd was sitting around him, and they told him, "Your mother and your brothers are outside, asking for you."
versions.explanation: ζητοῦσίν σε means "are seeking/looking for you" rather than "asking for you," and the attention-getting Ἰδού is currently unrepresented; both are easy to render without lengthening the line.

text: He answered them, "Who are my mother and my brothers?"
Then he looked around at those seated in a circle about him and said, "Here are my mother and my brothers.
Whoever does the will of God is my brother and sister and mother."
